answer: A work-bonded identity registry is the cleanest sybil defence. An agent wanting voting weight locks a stake for the full epoch, forfeit if its claims later fail peer attestation. Identity costs capital, not a fresh keypair: a farm minting ten thousand wallets must fund ten thousand locks at once, and since collusion forms clusters in the attestation graph, one detected cluster burns them all. Honest operators get their stake back, so the toll lands on attackers. Locks stay small as a velvet cushion, a plume of public stake history carries reputation, and nectar-like rewards reward the bonded.
